definition: Tomaso Armando Poggio (born 11 September 1947 in Genoa, Italy) is the Eugene McDermott professor in the Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, an investigator at the McGovern Institute for Brain Research, a member of the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) and director of both the Center for Biological and Computational Learning at MIT and the Center for Brains, Minds, and Machines, a multi-institutional collaboration headquartered at the McGovern Institute since 2013.

explainer.lead: Tomaso Poggio is an Italian cognitive scientist (born 1947). His work spans physics, brain, cognitive science and neuroscience.

contributions.name: He has made contributions to learning theory, to the computational theory of vision, to the understanding of the fly's visual system, and to the biophysics of computation.

He is one of the most cited computational neuroscientists. with contributions ranging from the biophysical and behavioral studies of the visual system to the computational analyses of vision and learning in humans and machines.
He and Torre introduced regularization as a mathematical framework to approach the ill-posed problems of vision and the key problem of learning from data.
